title: A living sacrifice (Romans 12:1–2)
hook: offer your bodies; be transformed by the renewing of your mind

segments.voice: Yesterday, the olive tree, and the wild olive grafted in against nature. Your line was you don't support the root.

Sacrifice. The word can bring up something dead: an animal on an altar, smoke going up. Or something given up: the sacrifice fly in baseball, the parent who works two jobs. Something lost so something else can happen. Now put together two words that don't seem to belong: a living sacrifice. For eleven chapters, Paul has talked about what God has done: grace, faith, the Spirit, super-conquering. Now he turns a corner. A small word in his first sentence ties what God has done to how to live. Then he asks for something strange.
screen: `SACRIFICE: SOMETHING DEAD, OR LOST.` → `ELEVEN CHAPTERS OF WHAT GOD HAS DONE.` → `NOW PAUL TURNS A CORNER.`

segments.voice: Here it is, in the King James Bible: "I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service." Start with therefore. Everything Paul asks from here grows out of the mercies of God he's already described. Not do this so God will love you, but God has loved you, therefore. Then bodies. Not just your soul, not just your Sunday: your hands, your feet, your tired back, your Tuesday afternoon. And a living sacrifice: not killed on an altar, but offered and still breathing, going on with ordinary life as a gift. The King James says reasonable service; the Greek can mean the worship that makes sense, or spiritual worship. Translators still argue about it. Then verse two: "And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind." Conformed: pressed into a shape, like dough in a mold. Transformed is a different kind of change. The Greek is metamorphousthe; you can hear metamorphosis in it, a caterpillar becoming a butterfly. It's the same word the Gospels use for Jesus on the mountain, when he was transfigured and shone. And it's passive: be transformed. Christians hear that as something God does, not something a person pulls off by effort. The change starts in the renewing of your mind, in what a person thinks about and dwells on. These two verses open the practical chapters that follow: worship that walks out of church on two feet.
screen: `THEREFORE: BECAUSE OF GOD'S MERCIES.` · `YOUR BODY, YOUR TUESDAY.` · `CONFORMED, OR TRANSFORMED.` · `METAMORPHOSIS: THE TRANSFIGURATION WORD.` · then, large: `BE YE TRANSFORMED BY THE RENEWING OF YOUR MIND.`

segments.voice: Picture the rest of your day, hour by hour: the commute, the meetings, the dishes, the kids, the errands, nothing special. Hold it all out in open hands as a gift, not a performance, and feel your feet on the floor and your hands, part of the offering too. If you pray, you can offer the day to God in your own words, or in silence.
Living sacrifice. Not something killed on an altar, but a whole ordinary life, body and all, offered to God as a gift.
Your line: be transformed. Not pressed into a mold, but made new. Day three hundred twenty-six.

howItsDone: Some Christians begin the day by offering it to God, and some traditions, such as the Catholic Morning Offering, have set prayers for this; Romans 12:1–2 is often memorized.

It means giving up everything fun, so that God will love you more.

chat.meaning: Paul says present your bodies a living sacrifice: not killed, but offered and still breathing, a gift that grows out of God's mercies.
